subject: latin
title: Latin Language
deck: The grammar of the Language paper, one lesson a point: what it is, how to spot it, how to translate it, and a short set of sentences to try. The vocabulary tester and the grammar gym pick up where each lesson leaves off.

items.title: The cases and what they do
items.desc: Nominative to ablative: the job each case does in a sentence.

items.title: Prepositions
items.desc: Which take the accusative, which the ablative, and in and sub with both.

items.title: Pronouns
items.desc: hic, ille, is, ipse, idem and the relative qui.

items.title: The tenses of the indicative
items.desc: Present, imperfect, future, perfect, pluperfect: forming and translating them.

items.title: The passive
items.desc: Present, imperfect and perfect passive, and the ablative of agent.

items.title: Irregular verbs
items.desc: sum, possum, eo, fero, volo, nolo, malo.

items.title: Participles
items.desc: Present, perfect passive and perfect active (deponent), and how to translate them.

items.title: The ablative absolute
items.desc: A noun and a participle in the ablative, standing apart from the sentence.

items.title: Purpose clauses
items.desc: ut and ne with the subjunctive: saying why something is done.

items.title: Result clauses
items.desc: tam, tantus, adeo ... ut: saying what came of it.

items.title: Indirect command
items.desc: Telling, asking and persuading with ut and ne.

items.title: Indirect statement
items.desc: Accusative and infinitive after verbs of saying, thinking and knowing.

items.title: Indirect question
items.desc: Question words with the subjunctive, and num and -ne.

items.title: cum clauses
items.desc: cum with the subjunctive: when, since, although.

items.title: Time clauses and conditionals
items.desc: dum, postquam, ubi, antequam, and si with the indicative.

items.title: Relative clauses
items.desc: qui, quae, quod: agreeing with its antecedent, taking its case from its own clause.

items.title: Translating a passage
items.desc: Finding the verb, keeping the clauses apart, and when to write it out.

items.title: The comprehension questions
items.desc: What the marks are for, and how much Latin to quote.
